settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: The class comment states it is 'just a simple test of how a HTML renderer could be like', suggesting it may be a demo/limited renderer rather than the primary REST output.
HtmlHelper does not itself acquire request or graph input; all parameters are passed by callers, so any injection requires an unexamined caller to pass untrusted data.
The output type is text/html; whether the identity of the injected data is attacker-controllable was not verified.
candidates.description:
community/server/src/main/java/org/neo4j/server/rest/domain/HtmlHelper.java constructs HTML documents by directly concatenating object data into the output StringBuilder without any observable HTML escaping. In start(...) the title parameter is inserted into and into a single-quoted id attribute (builder.append("<html><head><title>" + title + "" ...) and "... id='" + title.toLowerCase() + "'>"). In appendMessage(...) the message string is inserted into a

element. In append(...) for Map entries, keys and values are appended and caption/htmlClass are inserted into /. If any of these strings derive from user-controlled data (e.g., graph property values, property keys, labels, or request parameters surfaced by representations), stored or reflected HTML/JavaScript injection is possible. The candidate is the raw concatenation pattern and the absence of escaping at these sink lines; reachability from untrusted input and any upstream sanitization were not established.
missing_evidence: Confirmed caller data flow into HtmlHelper.start/append/appendMessage from untrusted input (HtmlFormat and Representation classes were not fully read).
Whether the HTML representation/format is enabled and reachable in default server configuration.
Whether any sanitizer/encoder is applied to property keys/values before rendering.
Whether Content-Type/headers or CSP mitigate the risk in practice.
preconditions: A code path renders user-controlled data through HtmlHelper (e.g., HtmlFormat rendering of a representation whose fields come from graph properties or request input).
No upstream sanitization/escaping is applied to those values before they reach HtmlHelper.
The HTML output format is reachable by an attacker who can influence the rendered data.
candidates.title: HtmlHelper builds HTML by raw string concatenation of graph-derived values (potential HTML/script injection)
